dedupe_keys.name: global land use 2015 to 2100 at 0 05 degrees under 15 ssp rcp scenarios gcam demeter chen and co authors 2020

description: This dataset projects global gridded land use from 2015 to 2100 at 0.05 degrees in 5-year steps under 15 SSP-RCP scenarios, each driven by five climate models. Min Chen, Chris Vernon, Neal Graham, Mohamad Hejazi, Maoyi Huang, Katherine Calvin and co-authors at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory's Joint Global Change Research Institute published it with a data descriptor in Scientific Data in October 2020. The Global Change Analysis Model provides regional land use and the Demeter model downscales it; two versions come from harmonised and original GCAM projections, each with results per climate model plus their mean and standard deviation. Results are broadly consistent with the Land Use Harmonization v2 dataset. Coverage is global except Antarctica. Format and access: self-describing NetCDF files via a PNNL DataHub DOI. Licence: not stated on the pages read; the article is open access; free. Caveats: 0.05-degree cells (about 5 km) are coarse for city work. It supports long-range land change inputs for exposure and green-blue infrastructure studies. Related catalogue records are the Chen, Li and Liu 1 km projections and the PLUM global land use scenarios.
